findings.quote: but the prior-year loss carried a large charge, so the narrower loss reflects that charge dropping out rather than a demand recovery
findings.issue: The grounding surface (MD&A Financial Summary) gives only the raw six-month net losses — $47.0M in H1'26 versus $310.3M in H1'25 — and never states that the prior-year loss contained a 'large charge.' Asserting that H1'25 'carried a large charge' and that the H1'26 narrowing 'reflects that charge dropping out' is an unsupported causal inference stated as established fact. It recurs at sections.financials.incomeCommentary ('the prior-year loss included a large charge, so the loss narrowed even though revenue fell'). The size of the H1'25 loss invites the inference, but the pack does not establish it.
findings.fix: Either drop the causal mechanism and state only what the pack supports — the net loss narrowed to $47.0M from $310.3M while revenue still fell, so the narrowing is not evidence of a demand recovery — or attribute the 'large charge' to a specific source in the pack. Do not assert the composition of the prior-year loss as fact in both analystCommentary and incomeCommentary.
findings.note: Fixed. analystCommentary now reads '...but revenue still fell over the same period, so the narrower loss is not evidence of a demand recovery.' incomeCommentary now reads '...since revenue declined over that span, the smaller loss should not be read as a sign that demand has recovered.' The 'large charge' causal claim is removed from both fields; only the pack-supported comparison remains.

findings.quote: Balance-sheet actions: a pending sale of Plant II assets and a nearly $38 million GM payment expected in Q1 2026.
findings.issue: The '$38 million GM payment expected in Q1 2026' is drawn from the DEF 14A 2025 Highlights filed March 27, 2026. This report is dated September 24, 2026, so Q1 2026 is roughly six months past. Presenting a Q1 2026 expectation as a forward-looking catalyst is stale dating: whether GM has paid is not in the pack, and a catalyst list implies events still ahead. sections.management.capitalAllocation handles the same fact more honestly in the past tense ('expected a nearly $38 million payment from GM in Q1 2026').
findings.fix: Move the GM payment out of the forward catalysts, or date it as a Q1 2026 expectation per the March 2026 proxy whose receipt the pack does not confirm. Reserve the catalyst slot for a genuinely forward item such as the Plant II asset sale, which the proxy still describes as being pursued.
findings.note: Fixed. catalysts[3] now reads 'Completion of the Plant II asset sale the company is pursuing, which would add cash and de-risk the balance sheet' — a genuinely forward item. The stale Q1 2026 GM payment is removed from the forward catalysts and now appears only in capitalAllocation in the past tense.

findings.quote: the company sold $168.9 million of PyroThin thermal barriers in 2025, down from $306.8 million in 2024 and $110.1 million in 2023, primarily to GM, with Toyota and Automotive Cells Company (ACC) also in production.
findings.issue: This sentence is repeated almost verbatim in sections.businessMoat.segments[0].body; the two sections also duplicate the thermal-runaway description and the 'East Providence... external facility in China... OPE fabrication operation in Mexico' manufacturing sentence. House style says no sentence appears in two sections. Two further cross-section duplications: sections.executiveSummary.catalysts[2] ('North Sea pipe-in-pipe subsea project with expected delivery in Q3 2026 and support of several LNG projects') is near-identical to sections.growth.points[1]; and the 'Volvo Cars (2027) and a leading American OEM (2028)' program pair appears in both sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body and catalysts[1] inside the same executive summary.
findings.fix: Keep each fact in the section that argues it and refer back in words elsewhere. Trim the businessMoat segment body to its moat argument (switching costs, no-minimum-commitments) rather than re-listing the PyroThin sales series and manufacturing footprint; let the growth point add mechanism the catalyst does not; and have the exec-summary catalyst point at the thesis rather than restate the Volvo/OEM years.
findings.note: Fixed. businessMoat.segments[0].body is now a moat argument (switching costs, no minimum commitments) with the PyroThin sales series and footprint removed; growth.points[1] now adds mechanism (steadier, less single-customer exposed) rather than repeating the North Sea/LNG catalyst; and catalysts[1] now points at the thesis ('the contracted PyroThin OEM programs discussed in the thesis') instead of restating the Volvo/OEM years.

findings.quote: the risk and reward are balanced
findings.issue: The page's own conviction row makes reward and risk asymmetric, not balanced: expected upside is +8.3% (weighted value ~$6.15 vs the $5.68 price) while bear-case downside is -42.8% ($3.25 vs $5.68), a reward/risk of 0.19x. sections.finalRecommendation states the opposite of 'balanced' — 'the reward-to-risk does not justify a positive rating.' The HOLD here follows from low expected upside (E below the +10% BUY threshold), not from balance between up and down, so calling risk and reward 'balanced' is incoherent with both the conviction numbers and the final recommendation.
findings.fix: Reword to match the numbers, e.g. 'modest expected upside is set against a much deeper bear case, so reward-to-risk is unattractive; we rate HOLD because expected value sits only slightly above the current price.' Align the analyst commentary with sections.finalRecommendation.
findings.note: Fixed. analystCommentary now reads 'modest expected upside is set against a much deeper bear case, so reward-to-risk is unattractive; we rate ASPN HOLD because expected value sits only slightly above the current price.' This matches the conviction row (E +8.3%, D -42.8%, R 0.19x) and sections.finalRecommendation.

findings.quote: The disclosed 5% stockholders are outside institutions: entities affiliated with Koch, Inc. own 14.83%, Oaktop Capital Management II 5.31% and Needham Investment Management and affiliates 5.25%.
findings.issue: The section reads the insider stake for the holder (2.96% group / 1.46% CEO -> alignment comes through at-risk pay) but only lists the 5% holders' percentages. Koch's 14.83% is a concentrated outside block roughly ten times the entire insider group and the single largest holder; the paragraph does not say what that block lets Koch do (significant influence, an anchor or potential activist position) versus a diffuse holder. Per rubric item 4, a control/ownership figure should be read for the holder, not merely stated.
findings.fix: Add a sentence reading the Koch 14.83% position for its governance/voting implication (an influential anchor holder well above management's combined stake), so the ownership picture reaches a view rather than a list.
findings.note: Still open. insiderOwnership is unchanged from round 1: the Koch 14.83% (plus Oaktop and Needham) is still only listed, and the only interpretive sentence reads the insider stake ('alignment comes mainly through at-risk compensation'), not the Koch block. No sentence yet reads the 14.83% for what it lets Koch do relative to the 2.96% insider group.

findings.quote: Aspen ended 2025 with approximately $159 million in cash and sits in a {+ net cash -} position, with net debt of -$66.3M against total debt of $90.6M.
findings.issue: Two different cash figures underlie one sentence without reconciliation: the '$159 million' cash is from the DEF 14A, while the -$66.3M net debt is derived from balance-sheet cash of ~$156.9M ($90.6M debt minus $156.9M cash = -$66.3M). As written, $159M cash less $90.6M debt implies about $68.4M net cash, not the stated $66.3M. Both figures are individually grounded, but the reader cannot reconcile them and the report does not flag the two cash bases (rubric item 8).
findings.fix: Use one cash basis in the sentence, or note that ~$159M is the company's rounded year-end figure while the net-debt calc uses reported cash of ~$156.9M. Avoid pairing the proxy's rounded cash with a precise net-debt figure derived from a different cash number.
findings.note: Still open. The balanceCommentary sentence is unchanged from round 1: it still pairs the proxy's rounded ~$159M cash with the -$66.3M net debt (which the balance-sheet table derives from ~$156.9M cash against $90.6M debt). The two cash bases are still neither reconciled to one figure nor flagged.
